Hi Emma — following up from last week's demo. I put together a concise Mutual Action Plan (attached) focused on capacity reservation / eval -> commit flow so we can lock in the Dedicated or Private runway you need without surprises. A few asks so we can size the MAP and propose lane-by-lane timelines: 

- Workload profile: expected peak concurrent requests (streams) and typical sequence lengths (tokens).
- Target model(s): if you plan to run a 70B decoder vs smaller ensemble, that materially changes GPU counts.
- Environment preference: Dedicated (Redwood-managed, isolated GPU pools) vs Private (VPC or on-prem).
- Acceptance criteria for the eval: latency P95 target, throughput target, and quality gate (sample prompts).

High-level proposal (draft):
1) Evaluation sprint (2 weeks): perf & quality on a 2-node staging pool; collect eval vectors.
2) Performance gate + decision: if passes, we start reservation commit.
3) Reservation & onboarding: Dedicated lead time ~8-12 weeks; Private (on-prem) typically 12-20 weeks depending on hardware procurement and SOC2/HSM work.

I attached a short MAP doc and an evaluation checklist to help you fill in the profile. If you can send the first two data points (workload profile + preferred model) by EOD Thu we'll scope the GPU pool recommendation and propose a commit window. 

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call to walk through the MAP.

—Jordan

- Target models: we want quality comparable to Llama-3-70B / mix of 1 instruction-tuned 70B model + a smaller 13B for lighter work.

- Acceptance criteria: P95 latency < 400ms for 1k tokens on the 70B path under 6 concurrent streams; throughput to handle 1000 reqs/day with burst tolerance. Quality gate: we will provide a 100-prompt eval set.

Proposed timeline from our side: Eval sprint May 24 — Jun 4; procurement/internal sign-off Jun 7 — Jun 18; commit by Jul 15. The procurement team will need lead time visibility for hardware and MSA. Attaching our internal eval checklist with some additional fields.

Jordan — quick sizing + lead-time notes from infra/procurement: 

Sizing suggestion (to meet P95 < 400ms at 1k tokens, 6 concurrent):
- Staging: 2 x H100-80GB (4-GPU staging pool total using 2 nodes with 2 GPUs each) running quantized 4-bit for the 70B model during eval (enables responsive latency and keeps cost low).
- Production Dedicated (initial commit): 16 x H100-80GB (4 nodes x 4 GPUs) configured with KV cache and batching tuned for typical 600-token median; autoscale policy to add burst capacity up to 24 GPUs when needed.

Lead times (us-west):
- Dedicated pool provisioning (Redwood-managed): engineering & capacity scheduling + accepted commit -> ~8–10 weeks typical if hardware available in region.
- Private on-prem: 14–18 weeks (hardware procurement, rack & networking, SOC2 evidence collection, KMS/HSM integration).

Staged approach: yes — start with 2-node staging for the eval (we can burst to hosted shared pool on heavier tests). After gate, convert staging nodes to part of the production pool and allocate additional reserved nodes to reach 16 GPUs within 6–10 weeks.

I'm attaching a ballpark reserve estimate CSV and a short checklist of gating artifacts (SOC2 evidence, IP whitelisting, PO/POC). We'll need procurement contact info from EdgeHealth early (procurement@edgehealth.com).

—Priyom
Attachments: bg-reserve-estimate.csv
